bHint: gain per 1 staked when you win; lose 1 when you lose
fHint: share of wealth bet each round
growthAria: Curve of the expected log-wealth growth per round as a function of the fraction bet. Maximum at f* = {{fStar}}; turns negative from {{f0}}. Current fraction {{f}}, growth {{g}}.
wealthAria: Fan of {{n}} wealth paths over {{bets}} rounds betting {{f}}. Final median {{median}}×, P5 {{p5}}×, P95 {{p95}}×.
obs: Kelly suggests betting {{fStar}} of wealth. You are at {{f}} ({{ratio}}× Kelly): expected growth of {{g}} per round, versus {{gStar}} at full Kelly. From {{f0}} on, growth turns negative and typical wealth shrinks, even with an edge. Half Kelly keeps about {{halfShare}} of the growth with much smaller drawdowns.
obsNoEdge: No edge: with p = {{p}} and a {{b}}:1 payoff, the bet's expected value is ≤ 0 and f* ≤ 0. The best fraction is not to bet; any f > 0 makes typical wealth shrink.
note: Synthetic bet with a known probability and independent outcomes. In markets p and b are estimated with error, which is why many people use fractional Kelly. Educational content, not investment advice.
formulaText: g(f) is the expected growth of log wealth per round: after T rounds the median wealth is close to eT·g(f). The maximum is f*; the curve is flat around it, so half Kelly gives up only ~25% of the growth. With a small edge, g returns to zero near 2f*.
